text:
Barcelona’s pursuit of Julián Álvarez came at a modest cost on Tuesday after the Spanish FA fined the club €602 (£503) following a complaint by Atlético Madrid over contact with the striker.
Atlético accused Barcelona of approaching the Argentine, whose contract runs until June 2030, without first notifying them in writing.
The sanction falls under Article 133 of the federation’s regulations. Atlético also complained to Fifa, which declared it had no jurisdiction over the case.
For Álvarez, the repair work has been rather more public.
The striker scored Atlético’s winner against Deportivo La Coruna on Saturday, finding the net for a second successive match as his side moved within two points of the La Liga leaders Barcelona, before apologising for expressing his desire to join their rivals.
“It was a mistake. I understand why the fans are angry. If I were a fan, I’d be angry too. Especially given how they’ve supported me since I arrived,” Álvarez said referring to an interview during the 2026 World Cup in which he said that he “wanted to fulfil his dream” of playing for Barcelona, triggering a transfer dispute that stretched through the summer transfer window.
Frequently booed by the home fans this season, Álvarez received a standing ovation from sections of the crowd after scoring on Saturday, a sign of a thawing relationship with the Metropolitano faithful.
digest_he:
התאחדות הכדורגל הספרדית הטילה קנס סמלי בסך 602 אירו על ברצלונה, בעקבות תלונה רשמית שהגישה אתלטיקו מדריד על כך שהקטלאנים יצרו קשר עם החלוץ חוליאן אלברס ללא הודעה מוקדמת בכתב לקבוצתו, המעבירה לו חוזה עד שנת 2030.

התלונה הוגשה בהתאם לתקנון הפדרציה, בעוד שתלונה מקבילה שהגישה אתלטיקו לפיפ
